title: Use-case evaluation intake stub (one line of <state>/use_cases/evaluation_set.jsonl)
description: Written by operating.use_case_intake for every new content version of a file delivered to the AGENTS site 'Ontology UseCases' folder. It is the documented input to the evaluation tooling: an eval-item generator (evals/oracle, held-out generator) reads these lines from the live state directory, turns a confirmed stub into plx-eval-item/v1 items with the stub's split, and never commits a held_out one. A stub is not evaluation truth: status stays stub_unconfirmed until a person confirms the outcome, questions, desired actions, locations and permissions. Split: split_for(case_id) in operating/use_case_intake.py, rule plx-use-case-split/v1 (sha256 of rule:case_id, first 8 hex digits mod 3 == 0 -> dev, else held_out; 1 dev per 2 held-out). It depends only on the stable drive-item case id, never on document text, so a re-upload keeps its split. Spans (known_outcome.span, questions[*].span) are [start, end) character offsets into the stored extraction text text_ref, decoded from its UTF-8 bytes without newline translation (mail text keeps CRLF; sha256 of those bytes: text_sha256); the record's accounting.parts[*].start/end say which part of the artifact a span falls in. draft is outcome_stated only when known_outcome.stated (a labelled, non-placeholder statement in text that was actually extracted), else no_stated_outcome: an outcome is never invented. artifact_complete is the record's accounting.complete: false means some part was unread or skipped by a cap, so the text (and any absence of an outcome) is partial. Validate with ontology/json_contract.py.

sha256.description: null when the original exceeded the intake cap and was not pinned.
